sources.title: Recent trends in global portfolio flows amid sovereign tensions in the euro area

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1252 establishing a framework for a secure and sustainable supply of critical raw materials
sources.observedPeriod: Legal benchmarks for 2030; strategic raw-material value chains
sources.revision: Binding regulation, Official Journal L 2024/1252. Article 5 benchmarks are EU capacities that approach or reach 10% extraction, 40% processing and 25% recycling of annual Union consumption; diversification aims for no one third country above 65%. By 2027 Commission is to set recycling-capacity benchmarks against relevant waste streams.
sources.units: Capacity shares of annual Union consumption; percent
sources.relevance: Source map only; mapped mechanisms: critical_minerals_production, refining_capacity, magnet_recycling_stock_flow. The source does not by itself prove a mechanism.
sources.sourceType: official statistical dataset, law, publication, company/project disclosure, or scholarly literature
sources.availabilityLimit: Legal capacity benchmarks are goals, not evidence of realized supply, utilization or feedstock. Benchmarks are per strategic raw material / chain stage, and denominators must be matched. Recycling capacity benchmark is distinct from actual end-of-life recycled input.

sources.title: Selected strategic projects under the Critical Raw Materials Act
sources.observedPeriod: First EU strategic-project selections under CRMA; project stages include extraction, processing, recycling and substitution
sources.revision: Commission approved 47 EU projects 2025-03-25; a separate 13 projects in third countries selected 2025-06-04. Project list may be updated as later selections occur.

sources.availabilityLimit: Designation confers strategic-project status and permitting/support facilitation; it does not certify financing close, construction completion, qualified feedstock, commercial throughput or target contribution.

sources.title: Material streams from wind energy decommissioning to 2050
sources.observedPeriod: JRC modeled EU wind-turbine material decommissioning through 2050 based on installations through 2023; permanent-magnet REEs and boron detail
sources.revision: JRC report EUR 40324, 2025; exact publication date not disclosed. Models future end-of-life flows, finding slow increase through 2030 and stronger growth thereafter; excludes future repowering in conservative estimates.
sources.units: Tonnes/year by material and year; turbine material intensity in kg/MW; report-specific scenarios
sources.relevance: Substantive official stock-flow source: cumulative installed wind capacity and asset lifetimes determine future end-of-life magnet waste; supports examining whether recycling capacity can be fed by actual retired magnets.
sources.sourceType: official statistical dataset, law, publication, company/project disclosure, or scholarly literature
sources.availabilityLimit: This concerns wind turbine stock only, not all EU magnets, EVs or e-waste. Technical recovery potential is not available feedstock: report distinguishes collection, disassembly and recycling steps and notes secondary REE streams may remain below growing demand. Exact publication date is not disclosed.
